# Robustness and Spike Experiment

*Generated by `python main.py robust` on 2026-11-13 01:36 (12.6 min on `cuda`). All numbers come from this run.*

## Set-up

- **Walk-forward evaluation:** the full procedure repeated in 4 rounds; each round trains only on data before its validation year and is tested on the following period.
| round | train | validation | test |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2022 | 2018-10-01 to 2020-12-31 | to 2021-12-31 | to 2022-12-31 |
| 2023 | 2018-10-01 to 2021-12-31 | to 2022-12-31 | to 2023-12-31 |
| 2024 | 2018-10-01 to 2022-12-31 | to 2023-12-31 | to 2024-12-31 |
| 2025-2026 | 2018-10-01 to 2023-12-31 | to 2024-12-31 | to 2026-10-31 |

- **Main model:** GRU with `pollution+weather` inputs (`level_small`), as chosen on 2024 validation by `python main.py extended`.
- **Spike-weighted GRU:** each training day counts in proportion to (AQI / average AQI) ^ gamma, gamma from [1.0, 2.0] chosen per round on that round's validation year by the error on its most polluted 20% of days.
- **Ensemble:** the average of GRU (`pollution+weather`), LSTM (`pollution`), Transformer (`pollution`), XGBoost (`pollution+weather`).
- **Alert probability:** a GRU classifier for P(AQI > 200); the alert threshold is chosen on each round's validation year.
- Settings come from 2024 validation, so rounds 1-3 test years the choices never saw (round 3 tests 2024, the year those settings were chosen on, so it slightly favours the models). Round 4 re-scores the 2025-2026 test period already reported by `extended`.

## Does the model win every year? (test MAE, then difference vs persistence [95% interval])

| round | test days | persistence | GRU | Spike-weighted GRU | Ensemble |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2022 | 364 | 18.6 | 14.6, -4.0 [-6.1, -2.1] (better) | 21.6, +3.0 [+0.1, +6.2] (worse) | 14.2, -4.3 [-6.2, -2.5] (better) |
| 2023 | 365 | 19.5 | 15.1, -4.4 [-6.7, -2.6] (better) | 19.9, +0.4 [-1.8, +2.4] | 14.9, -4.5 [-6.5, -2.8] (better) |
| 2024 | 366 | 17.0 | 13.4, -3.7 [-5.1, -2.0] (better) | 18.1, +1.0 [-1.1, +3.3] | 13.1, -3.9 [-5.4, -2.3] (better) |
| 2025-2026 | 669 | 13.8 | 11.8, -2.0 [-3.2, -0.7] (better) | 12.8, -1.0 [-2.3, +0.3] | 10.9, -2.9 [-3.9, -1.9] (better) |

Rounds where each model is clearly better than persistence: GRU 4 of 4, Spike-weighted GRU 0 of 4, Ensemble 4 of 4.

All 1764 test days pooled: GRU -3.2 [-4.0, -2.4] (better); Spike-weighted GRU +0.5 [-0.4, +1.6]; Ensemble -3.8 [-4.5, -3.0] (better).

## High-pollution alerts (AQI > 200), F1 score

| round | high days | persistence | GRU | Ensemble | alert probability | caught (probability) | Brier score | threshold (from validation) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2022 | 68 | 0.815 | 0.845 | 0.849 | 0.810 | 64/68 | 0.079 | 0.65 |
| 2023 | 46 | 0.796 | 0.800 | 0.788 | 0.796 | 43/46 | 0.067 | 0.75 |
| 2024 | 42 | 0.738 | 0.740 | 0.795 | 0.701 | 34/42 | 0.073 | 0.75 |
| 2025-2026 | 41 | 0.585 | 0.723 | 0.713 | 0.619 | 30/41 | 0.065 | 0.8 |

The Brier score measures how well the probabilities match reality (0 = perfect; lower is better). n/a = no high days, or no alerts raised, in that period.

## How to read these results honestly

- Each round has a different number of polluted days; early years were dirtier than recent ones.
- Settings were chosen once, on 2024; they were not re-tuned per round.
- Round 4 re-uses the 2025-2026 test period, which was already scored once.
